\section*{Question 6}

Let \(f\) be a function defined by \(f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll}1-2 \sin x & \text { for } x \leq 0 \\ e^{-4 x} & \text { for } x>0\end{array}\right.\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Show that \(f\) is continuous at \(x=0\).
\item[(b)] For \(x \neq 0\), express \(f^{\prime}(x)\) as a piecewise-defined function. Find the value of \(x\) for which \(f^{\prime}(x)=-3\).
\item[(c)] Find the average value of \(f\) on the interval [-1, 1].
\item[(a)] \(\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}}(1-2 \sin x)=1\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& \lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}} e^{-4 x}=1 \\
& f(0)=1
\end{aligned}
\]
So, \(\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} f(x)=f(0)\).
Therefore \(f\) is continuous at \(x=0\).
\item[(b)] \(f^{\prime}(x)= \begin{cases}-2 \cos x & \text { for } x<0 \\ -4 e^{-4 x} & \text { for } x>0\end{cases}\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& -2 \cos x \neq-3 \text { for all values of } x<0 \\
& -4 e^{-4 x}=-3 \text { when } x=-\frac{1}{4} \ln \left(\frac{3}{4}\right)>0
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore \(f^{\prime}(x)=-3\) for \(x=-\frac{1}{4} \ln \left(\frac{3}{4}\right)\).
\item[(c)]
\[
\begin{aligned}
\int_{-1}^{1} f(x) d x & =\int_{-1}^{0} f(x) d x+\int_{0}^{1} f(x) d x \\
& =\int_{-1}^{0}(1-2 \sin x) d x+\int_{0}^{1} e^{-4 x} d x \\
& =[x+2 \cos x]_{x=-1}^{x=0}+\left[-\frac{1}{4} e^{-4 x}\right]_{x=0}^{x=1} \\
& =(3-2 \cos (-1))+\left(-\frac{1}{4} e^{-4}+\frac{1}{4}\right)
\end{aligned}
\]
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text { Average value } & =\frac{1}{2} \int_{-1}^{1} f(x) d x \\
& =\frac{13}{8}-\cos (-1)-\frac{1}{8} e^{-4}
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{itemize}
